hints: Look closely at the name PVC, poly(chloroethene), and ask yourself which atoms must be present in the polymer chain.
Since PVC contains carbon, hydrogen and chlorine, complete combustion must give more than just $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, think what the chlorine becomes.
Connect that chlorine-containing product to acidity in water and to which carbon product is a known greenhouse gas.
walkthrough:
**Recall what PVC is made from**

Think of PVC as a long chain built from chloroethene, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl}$. That means every repeat unit contains C, H and Cl.

Repeat unit: $$-(\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl})_n-$$

**Predict products of complete combustion**

Complete combustion in excess oxygen turns C to $\text{CO}_2$ and H to $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, but Cl cannot vanish. It forms hydrogen chloride gas, $\text{HCl}$.

Simplified idea: $$\text{C, H, Cl + O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{HCl}$$

**Link products to the statements**

$\text{CO}_2$ is a well known greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming, so a warming gas is indeed made. $\text{HCl}$ is acidic and hazardous, so it dissolves in scrubber water to make it acidic, not alkaline, and the exhaust gases must be treated.

options.A: Correct. Complete combustion of PVC produces $\text{CO}_2$ from its carbon content, and $\text{CO}_2$ is a major greenhouse gas contributing to global warming.
options.B: Incorrect. This is the trap of treating PVC like a hydrocarbon. Because PVC contains chlorine, $\text{HCl}$ is also formed in addition to $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
options.C: Incorrect. The exhaust contains acidic $\text{HCl}$ gas. When it dissolves in scrubber water it forms hydrochloric acid, so the water becomes acidic, not alkaline.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{HCl}$ is corrosive, acidic and hazardous to health and the environment. Exhaust gases from PVC burning must be scrubbed and treated, they cannot be released untreated.
